content:
alice.nguyen: Heads-up — nightly evals show a drop in context QA pass rate for v13b after yesterday's weight + tokenizer push. Batch summary attached in CI.
ben_ramirez: saw that. Which prompts are failing most? short-context vs long-context?
alice.nguyen: mostly long-context prompt set 'legal_longform_v2' and some multi-turn summarization cases. Failures are hallucinations / dropped entities.
dylan_eval: metric diff: EM down 8.6%, F1 down 6.1 on legal_longform_v2. For multi-turn, answer truncation / repetition increased.
chloe_ops: any infra changes? GPU driver or KV cache patch today?
alice.nguyen: no infra changes. The only things in the deploy were: v13b weights (quantized int8-opt) + tokenizer merge (new merges.json) + runtime patch for kv eviction order (tiny change).
ben_ramirez: tokenizer merge could shift tokenization offsets — might break prefix-based KV lookups or rollout comparisons.
dylan_eval: quick check: I diffed token counts on a sample of 100 prompts: ~12% had different tokenization boundaries, mostly splitting punctuation-adjacent tokens.
alice.nguyen: suspect: two things interacting: (1) tokenizer splits cause different key placements in KV cache leading to misaligned past key retrieval, (2) quantization + kernel selection causing subtle attention scale changes.
chloe_ops: any repro on a single GPU locally? I can spin a debug job.
ben_ramirez: try reproducing minimal case: take one long prompt that failed, run v12b and v13b tokenization + generation with kv debug prints.
alice.nguyen: here's the failing example (sanitized): "On April 12th, Company X acquired..." When tokenized with v12b it's 128 tokens, with v13b 132. Under v13b generation we see the model repeat 'Company X acquired' mid-answer.
dylan_eval: I ran a generation with kv debug on both. Logs show that under v13b the kv positions for token index 48..55 are off by +1 compared to v12b. That matches the 4-token delta.
ben_ramirez: that would explain misaligned attention windows — older prefix keys shifted so attention attends to wrong tokens intermittently.
chloe_ops: kv eviction order change mention — was that intended? It was a small fix but could interact with token offsets.
alice.nguyen: yes the runtime patch changed eviction to use insertion-order rather than LRU for ties. It was meant to reduce jitter. Maybe with different token boundaries the cache interactions changed.
ben_ramirez: proposal: revert runtime kv eviction change in a canary, and/or roll back tokenizer merge to old merges.json, then run nightly subset.
dylan_eval: I'll queue a canary: two jobs — (A) v13b weights + new tokenizer + runtime revert, (B) v13b weights + old tokenizer + runtime patch. That isolates tokenizer vs runtime.
chloe_ops: ETA for canaries? I can launch now, should finish in ~25m for our 1k prompt subset.
alice.nguyen: thanks. Also add a qualitative eval: dump logits for the mismatched region and softmaxed attention across past tokens.
dylan_eval: added request. Also tagging eva-bot to bump priority.
eva-bot: @channel CI job queued: canary-A (id: ci-1948765501), canary-B (id: ci-1948765502). Notifying owners.
ben_ramirez: good. Meanwhile, I'm running a local tokenizer diff script to map boundary shifts back to merges. I'll post the top 15 merges that changed mapping.
alice.nguyen: if tokenizer merges are the root cause, we need to consider pinning tokenizer for v13b until we vet merges, and include tokenization diffs in release checklist.
chloe_ops: Agreed. Also adding a runtime revert flag so Dedicated customers can opt-out of eviction change if they hit this.
ben_ramirez: quick check: quantization often affects token logits magnitude but doesn't shift KV positions. So quantization alone unlikely to cause boundary shifts, but can amplify errors once KV misalignment occurs.
alice.nguyen: exactly. Would like to see canary results before deciding rollback order.
dylan_eval: canary-A finished: EM drop reduced to 1.2% (much better). canary-B finished: EM drop still ~7.9%.
ben_ramirez: strong signal: runtime eviction change is the main culprit interacting with tokenizer changes.
alice_nguyen: ok action items: 1) revert eviction-order change immediately from prod (chloe) 2) run full nightly with runtime revert + v13b (dylan) 3) freeze tokenizer merges until we do targeted merge audit (ben) 4) draft postmortem note for release channel (alice)
chloe_ops: reverting now to previous eviction behavior for hosted and dedicated canaries, will roll above today.
ben_ramirez: I'll produce the merge-audit script and a small report showing problematic merges and sample tokenizations.
dylan_eval: scheduling full nightly run once revert is live. Will monitor rollouts and keep this thread updated.
alice.nguyen: thanks all. After we confirm stable, we'll iterate on a proper KV compatibility test in our nightly to catch this earlier.
chloe_ops: +1. Also will add a flag in runtime to enable per-customer eviction policy override.
eva-bot: Update: revert deployed to canary pool at 1948765760. Monitoring metrics.
alice.nguyen: noting timeline for the postmortem: start: 1948765400 (when regression first appeared), mitigated: 1948765760 (revert deployed). I'll draft and share in #eng-ml later today. :memo:
ben_ramirez: can we add a unit test that asserts tokenization delta <= 2 tokens across merge updates for our canonical prompt subsets?
alice_nguyen: yes add that to model-onboarding checklist. ok closing for now, will reopen if any regressions reappear. :white_check_mark:
